question: does the masking effect survive replacing the mask token with an uninformative in-distribution value, which would make it information removal rather than an off-distribution query

layout.softmax_over: the supplied gene positions, so a response is a share of the cell's counts and depends on which genes were supplied together
layout.input_order: ascending vocabulary position; the model carries no gene positional encoding, so the order is a convention, not a constraint

conditions.visible: the read-out gene sees its own input value
conditions.masked: the read-out gene's input replaced by the model's own mask convention (boolean_mask_argument, value None)
conditions.median_substituted: the read-out gene's input replaced by one uninformative in-distribution level, the same scalar for every hidden gene

substitute_level.over: the pooled non-targeting control level of the read-out genes of this cell line
substitute_level.why: one scalar for every hidden gene, so it carries no gene-specific information, and a level half the read-out set already sits below, so no input value leaves the distribution the model was trained to read

mask_spec.source: scPrint.forward(mask=...); the value encoder zeroes the expression embedding at masked positions. The checkpoint records no pretraining mask rate, so 0.15 is used and recorded as a fallback

read_depth.note: the mask convention leaves the input's total unchanged, the substitution does not; both the baseline and the perturbed pass of a condition carry the same total, so the response difference is taken at one fixed background

value_grid_note: the zero-out query the comparison is about, plus the top of the production grid so the reading is not specific to zero-out
perturbed_subset: the in_masked subset of run 2's 250-gene block, reproduced from the same seed (42) and scope, so the numbers sit beside the masked block already extracted

coverage.selection_rule: stratified sample of 250 at seed 42, 125 per stratum, drawn from the in-scope set; the individual-cell and masked subsets are nested inside it
coverage.in_scope_definition: perturbations in strata S3, S4_highest whose target gene is also a read-out gene of this cell line, so it can be perturbed at all
coverage.comparability_note: a block at partial coverage and a block at full coverage share the perturbed genes of the smaller one but not its row order; join on perturbed_gene_id, never on row index, and do not compare a per-block aggregate across two different coverages

estimator_correction: a mask block that also hides the perturbed gene overwrites the perturbation, so that pass contributes exactly zero; those passes are skipped here and averaged in by run 2's masked block, whose estimator is reproduced as abs_median_run2_diluted_estimator

visible.note: the read-out gene's own value is visible; no block cycling is needed because the response does not depend on the mask partition

masked.note: read only where the gene is hidden, averaged over the cycles in which the perturbed gene was not hidden in the same block

median_substituted.note: read only where the gene is hidden, averaged over the cycles in which the perturbed gene was not hidden in the same block
